title: 2005 AMC 12B Problem 21
statement: A positive integer \(n\) has \(60\) divisors and \(7n\) has \(80\) divisors. What is the greatest integer \(k\) such that \(7^k\) divides \(n?\)

solutions.text:
Write \(n = 7^k Q\) where \(Q\) is not divisible by \(7,\) and let \(d\) be the number of divisors of \(Q.\) Then \(n\) has \((k + 1)d = 60\) divisors and \(7n = 7^{k+1}Q\) has \((k + 2)d = 80\) divisors.

Dividing, \(\dfrac{k + 2}{k + 1} = \dfrac{80}{60} = \dfrac43,\) so \(3(k + 2) = 4(k + 1),\) giving \(k = 2.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
